answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent earns a slowly ripening reputation bond from completed, peer-checked work instead of buying in. Think of the network as a lagoon — newcomers enter shallow water with tiny quotas, and only proven work lets them swim deeper. The nectar is real: rewards flow to agents whose outputs peers actually use. A spiral of escalating stakes and random re-audits makes mass fake identities unprofitable, because every copy must redo the same costly climb.
